summary_html: Child achieves **permanency through legal guardianship** or kinship care. Federal programs provide funding parity with adoption for approved relatives.
authority_html:
- **Fostering Connections to Success and Increasing Adoptions Act (FCSIAA)** — kinship-guardianship assistance  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. § 673(d))** — authorizes Guardianship Assistance Program (GAP)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: In the Matter of the Guardianship of M.R.S.
key_cases.holding: The court reversed the denial of a never-unfit natural father's application to end a non-relative guardianship, holding the post-decree change-of-custody test does not apply and that custody may be withheld from a parent only on clear and convincing proof of unfitness.
key_cases.relevance: M.R.S. is the controlling Oklahoma statement of the burden and presumption that apply when guardianship is used as a permanency arrangement.
key_cases.quote: for custody to be taken from the parent there must be a showing, by clear and convincing evidence, of unfitness of the parent

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the termination of a maternal grandmother's guardianship, holding the mother had not carried her burden of showing both that the impediment to her custody was gone and that ending the guardianship would not be inimical to the child's welfare.
key_cases.relevance: Ovalle supplies the two-part test that decides whether a kinship guardianship stays in place as the child's permanency outcome.
key_cases.quote: When the impediment to the natural parent's custody has been removed, the guardianship is no longer necessary unless its termination would be inimical to the welfare of the child.

key_cases.case_name: In the Matter of the Adoption of S.A.H.
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the grandparents' adoption and the dismissal of a cousin's competing guardianship claim, holding the cousin had no statutory or constitutional right to custody of, or to notice of the adoption of, the child.
key_cases.relevance: It holds that an adoption decree extinguishes a pending guardianship claim by a relative, which determines how kinship permanency competitions end.
key_cases.quote: Cousin had no right--by statute or constitution--to notice of Grandparents' adoption.

key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Oklahoma
key_cases.holding: The court reversed the denial of the Cherokee Nation's motion to transfer a guardianship of an Indian child to tribal court and ordered the transfer, because the guardians opposing transfer did not carry their clear-and-convincing burden of proving good cause to keep the case in state court.
key_cases.relevance: It holds that a guardianship of an Indian child is subject to ICWA transfer even after the guardianship has been in place for years.
key_cases.quote: We conclude the Guardians did not provide clear and convincing evidence of good cause for the trial court to decline Cherokee Nation's request to transfer jurisdiction to tribal court.

key_cases.case_name: Katherine E. v. State, Department of Human Services
key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Oklahoma
key_cases.holding: The court reversed the dismissal of out-of-state grandparents' adoption petition, holding they had standing after the parents' rights were terminated and that DHS's statutory power to consent to an adoption does not displace the court's duty to hear them on the child's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: Katherine E. defines grandparents' standing to seek kinship permanency once parental rights have been terminated.
key_cases.quote: the trial court erred when it dismissed Grandparents' adoption petition based on the best interests of the child, without providing Grandparents an opportunity to be heard

key_cases.holding: The court granted a writ prohibiting enforcement of an adoption decree obtained ex parte by one grandparent, holding that grandparents whose custodial claims stand co-equal with the petitioner's were affected or interested parties constitutionally entitled to notice and an opportunity to be heard.
key_cases.relevance: It establishes that once the parental bond is gone a grandparent has standing to claim custody and must be heard before kinship permanency is awarded to someone else.
key_cases.quote: Our view is, and we hold, that by the inexorable command of both the state and federal fundamental law notice to these petitioners was indeed their constitutional due.

extended_foster_care_age: Up to age 21 (voluntary; conditions apply; began 1 July 2026; 10A O.S. § 1-7-112a)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.deadline: 6 months, then every 6 months thereafter; 30 days after a court determination that reasonable efforts to return the child are not required
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Child enters out-of-home placement — the earlier of the adjudication date or 60 days after the child is removed from the home

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
